cases.expected_user_explanation: Within Hanafi's 3-10 day haid range, prior purity exceeds the 15-day minimum.
Exactly at Hanafi's 72-hour (3-day) minimum — classified as haid, not below it.
One minute short of Hanafi's minimum — does not qualify as haid; requires further guidance rather than a default classification.
Exactly at Shafi'i's 15-day maximum — still classified as haid.
One minute past Shafi'i's 15-day maximum — exceeds the boundary; the engine does not classify this as a distinct istihada state (see FIQH-6), only as needsAdvisory.
cases.disputed_note: The engine collapses 'beyond maximum duration' into the same needsAdvisory state used for 'below minimum' and other ambiguous cases (see FIQH-6) -- whether this specific case should instead route to a distinct istihadah-aware state is a genuine open question for reviewer judgment, not merely a boundary-arithmetic check.

cases.expected_user_explanation: Not enough logged history to establish a baseline — the engine does not attempt a classification.

Within Maliki's general 1-15 day range and thus classified haid by this engine's current logic; the engine separately reports the bleeding exceeded her previously-established 6-day personal habit (isWithinPersonalHabit=false) as informational context, not as a factor changing the classification itself.
cases.disputed_note: Whether exceeding a previously-established personal habit should be purely informational (current behavior) or should itself affect classification is a genuine fiqh question specific to the Maliki 'adah framework, not resolved by this session.

cases.expected_user_explanation: Hanafi-specific rule: prior purity is one minute short of the 15-day minimum required before a new haid can be confirmed, even though the bleeding duration itself is otherwise valid.
No current bleeding recorded — classified as a state of purity (tuhr).

The identical raw bleeding episode (30 hours, same start date) produces a different classification depending solely on the user's selected madhhab — demonstrating the engine's madhhab-sensitivity is real and reachable, and that raw facts never change, only the applied rule does.
cases.disputed_note: Included specifically because it demonstrates real cross-madhhab disagreement on IDENTICAL facts -- not a defect, but exactly the kind of case a reviewer should examine most closely to confirm each madhhab's own position is correctly applied.

inputs.note: Nifas is NOT handled by MadhhabRuleEvaluator/FiqhCycleState at all — it is computed by a structurally separate engine (PregnancyStatusEngine, feeding FiqhReportInsights.nifas). This case documents that separation rather than exercising MadhhabRuleEvaluator.

cases.expected_user_explanation: Postpartum/nifas status is derived from pregnancy_profile's is_postpartum/postpartum_start_date fields via a separate state machine, prioritized ahead of cycle-state logic in the Fiqh Report. This case is recorded to make the architectural boundary explicit for reviewers, not to exercise a specific numeric threshold.
cases.disputed_note: Documents an architectural boundary (nifas handled by a separate engine) rather than a numeric threshold -- flagged as needing reviewer confirmation that this separation itself is fiqh-appropriate, not just that the code is internally consistent.

cases.expected_user_explanation: Deliberately constructed to fail on two independent grounds at once (bleeding duration below minimum AND prior purity below minimum) — engine still correctly resolves to a single needsAdvisory state rather than a contradictory or undefined result; it does not report which of the two grounds triggered it, only that advisory guidance is needed.
